value.author: samMularczyk
value.layerInfo: A gradient blended from colour spots, warped by waves.

colorCount: How many stops are used. This is also the SPOT COUNT - each colour is one spot in the field.
positions: Slides every spot along its own path. A seed, not a count - changing it rearranges the composition without changing how many spots there are.
swirl: Twists the field about its centre, strongest there and falling away with distance. It breathes slowly rather than holding a fixed angle, so it never settles.
mixing: Does two things at once, which is why one slider covers the whole range: it sets the distance falloff exponent and how sharply the nearest spot wins. Low gives hard stripes, high a gradual blend.
waveX: Sine distortion across the field, strongest through the middle and calm at the border.
waveY: The same on the other axis.
waveYShift: Phase offset of the vertical wave.
grainMixer: Eats into each spot's reach, so the boundaries between colours break up rather than staying clean.
grainOverlay: Noise laid over the finished gradient.
rotation: Rotates the whole field, in degrees.
evolution: Drives everything that moves, in degrees. Keyframe it, or drive it with a Frame behaviour - the rate is yours rather than tied to the comp clock.
loop: Makes the field return exactly to its start, so it can be cycled with no visible seam.
cycles: How many full revolutions of Evolution before it repeats. At 2 the field comes home at Evolution 720, not 360 - so a higher count travels further through the noise and gives more variation before the repeat.
